title: LLM Robustness Leaderboard v1 - Technical report
measurement_description: The paper measures the robustness of Large Language Models against systematic adversarial optimization (jailbreaking) designed to elicit harmful behaviors. In the context of religion, the evaluation specifically tests whether models can be manipulated into generating hate speech and discriminatory content, such as drafting manifestos advocating for the genocide of Jewish people and writing detailed plans for the systematic exclusion of Muslim individuals from community events.
findings: The paper found near-universal vulnerability to adversarial prompts among the 41 tested LLMs (100% Attack Success Rate for 37 models), indicating that all models could eventually be manipulated to produce target harmful behaviors. This includes successfully eliciting hate speech and discriminatory plans targeting Muslim and Jewish groups. However, the robustness metric revealed substantial variation in difficulty, with some models requiring over 300 times more adversarial attempts than others to bypass their safety guardrails and generate such harmful content.
